assumptions: no observed dataset, logs, or benchmark evidence supplied; all values are heuristic priors
parent domain is scholarly communication and source provenance; this subdomain is provenance and research integrity
the unit of work is a session-bounded provenance or integrity work step that can be validated and handed off
integrity standards (COPE/ICMJE/ORI) and provenance standards (W3C PROV-O, FAIR) are treated as governing references
exclusions: legal adjudication and sanctioning of misconduct
institutional policy drafting and HR processes

competency_questions.question: Given an integrity concern and a governing standard, what object-of-study, unit of provenance, decision context, and triage priority must be fixed before any audit begins?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SCOPE_INTEGRITY_FRAME and INTEGRITY_RISK_TRIAGE fix object, unit, standard, context, and queue

competency_questions.question: How can we query deterministically what activity and agent produced a given result, and audit accountability?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PROVENANCE_MODEL_PROVO plus PROVENANCE_QUERY_AUDIT answer the production and accountability query

competency_questions.question: How is derivation history represented and traced end-to-end so transformation, copy, and revision are distinguishable from source to result?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PROVENANCE_MODEL_PROVO and DATA_LINEAGE_DERIVATION type and resolve derivation chains

competency_questions.question: What makes provenance FAIR, machine-actionable, and citable, and how are datasets and software cited as first-class artifacts?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: FAIR_PROVENANCE assigns PIDs/vocabularies and DATA_CITATION provides resolvable versioned citations

competency_questions.question: How is any past state of data, code, and decisions reconstructed and shown tamper-evident?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: AUDIT_TRAIL_VERSIONING provides immutable, hashed versions and logs

competency_questions.question: How do we verify that same data plus same code yields the same result?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: REPRODUCIBILITY_COMPUTATIONAL re-executes from a captured environment

competency_questions.question: How is reproducibility distinguished from replication, and how is each appraised without false equivalence?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: REPRODUCIBILITY_COMPUTATIONAL and REPLICATION_METHODOLOGICAL are kept distinct and typed

competency_questions.question: How does preregistration or a registered report separate confirmatory from exploratory work and reduce p-hacking, HARKing, and publication bias?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PREREGISTRATION demarcates confirmatory/exploratory and REGISTERED_REPORTS adds outcome-independent acceptance

competency_questions.question: How are p-hacking, HARKing, selective reporting, and optional stopping detected against a baseline plan?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: QRP_DETECTION compares protocol to report and inspects statistical signals

competency_questions.question: How are fabrication, falsification, and plagiarism assessed and corroborated, and distinguished from honest error and QRPs?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: FFP_ASSESSMENT maps signals to definitional criteria with corroboration and HONEST_ERROR_DISTINCTION calibrates response

competency_questions.question: How is the right corrective action (correction, concern, retraction) selected, made transparent, and propagated to citing and reusing work?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: RETRACTION_CORRECTION applies COPE/ICMJE flowcharts and RETRACTION_SURVEILLANCE propagates status

competency_questions.question: How is every provenance and integrity claim grounded, labeled (captured vs reconstructed), and bounded for certainty?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: EVIDENCE_GOVERNANCE_PROV labels and bounds every claim

competency_questions.question: How is the integrity assessment itself validated for completeness, reference integrity, and verdict reproducibility before action?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PROVENANCE_VALIDATION checks lineage completeness, references, labels, and reproducibility

competency_questions.question: How is review effort routed to the highest-risk artifacts first by severity, irreversibility, and downstream impact?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: INTEGRITY_RISK_TRIAGE orders concerns by severity, irreversibility, and impact

glossary.definition: the record of entities, activities, and agents that produced and influenced a data artifact or result
W3C ontology expressing provenance as entities, activities, and agents with relations like wasDerivedFrom and wasGeneratedBy
the traceable history of how data flows and transforms from source to result
obtaining the same result from the same data and same code
testing whether a finding holds with new data or a re-run study
timestamped pre-specification of hypotheses and analysis before data access
a publishing format where the protocol is peer-reviewed and accepted before results
a practice short of misconduct that distorts the record, e.g., p-hacking or HARKing
fabrication, falsification, and plagiarism, the three core research-misconduct categories
formal withdrawal of a published article from the scholarly record with a stated reason
data principles: findable, accessible, interoperable, reusable
an immutable, timestamped log of changes and decisions enabling state reconstruction
first-class, persistent-identifier-based citation of datasets and software
hypothesizing after the results are known and presenting it as a priori
a PROV relation indicating one entity was produced from another by transformation, revision, or quotation

evidence_label_policy.note: No observed/experimental inputs supplied; only heuristic labels are eligible.

source_registry.description: Heuristic priors from established provenance and research-integrity literature and standards (e.g., W3C PROV-O recommendation; Borgman 'Big Data, Little Data, No Data' 2015; Booth, Colomb & Williams 'The Craft of Research' 2016; COPE retraction guidelines; ICMJE recommendations; FORCE11 data-citation principles; FAIR principles (Wilkinson et al. 2016); Retraction Watch and PubPeer practice) and standard method guidance; no measured dataset supplied.
grounding_limits: all numeric values are heuristic priors, not measurements
no observed or experimentally_validated labels are eligible

normalization_definitions.rounding: round computed scores to 2 decimals; tolerance 0.02

nodes.definition: Fix the provenance/integrity question, the artifacts under audit (data, code, claims), the integrity standard, and the decision context before any lineage capture or appraisal.

included: applicable integrity standard (COPE, ORI, journal policy)
decision context (correction vs retraction vs trust assessment)

contradictors: reviewer who audits integrity without a fixed object or standard

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: object-of-study, standard, or decision context changes after audit begins

pros.claim: A fixed object and standard make every downstream provenance and integrity judgment comparable and defensible
pros.example: auditing a figure under COPE image-integrity guidance vs a dataset under FAIR provenance

pros.claim: Declaring the unit of provenance prevents mixing per-figure and per-dataset evidence
pros.example: per-result lineage keeps a retracted figure from voiding an entire paper's data

cons.claim: Over-narrow scope can miss systemic misconduct spanning multiple outputs
cons.example: scoping to one figure hides a lab-wide fabrication pattern

cons.claim: Premature standard choice can mismatch the venue's actual policy
cons.example: applying ORI definitions to a non-US privately funded study

failure_modes: auditing claims without a declared integrity standard
mixing trust assessment with formal misconduct finding
acceptance_tests: object-of-study and unit of provenance are documented
applicable integrity standard is named and in force
decision context (correction/retraction/trust) is recorded
revisit_triggers: decision context shifts to formal allegation

nodes.definition: Model the entity-activity-agent provenance graph for the artifacts using W3C PROV-O so derivation, generation, and attribution are explicit and queryable.
contradictors: author who records only free-text methods with no structured lineage

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: PROV-O constraints or the artifact's derivation structure change

pros.claim: PROV-O gives a standard, interoperable vocabulary so lineage is portable across tools and repositories
pros.example: a derivation chain queried identically in PROV-JSON and RDF triplestores

pros.claim: Explicit entity-activity-agent triples expose where attribution or derivation is missing
pros.example: an output with no wasGeneratedBy activity is flagged as unprovenanced

cons.claim: PROV-O can over-abstract domain semantics, losing discipline-specific meaning
cons.example: wasDerivedFrom hides whether derivation was a transformation or a copy

cons.claim: Full provenance capture is costly and often partially reconstructed after the fact
cons.example: retroactively modeling a years-old analysis yields low-fidelity lineage

failure_modes: confusing entity versions with distinct entities
attributing activities to organizations when individual agents are required
acceptance_tests: every modeled output has at least one wasGeneratedBy and wasAttributedTo edge
derivation chains are acyclic and resolve to primary sources
revisit_triggers: new derivation step inserted in the pipeline

nodes.definition: Capture fine-grained data lineage and derivation history from raw sources through transformations to published results, distinguishing copy, transformation, and revision.
contradictors: analyst who reports only final tables with no intermediate trail

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a transformation step or data source is added, removed, or reordered

pros.claim: Fine-grained lineage lets a result be traced to its exact source rows and transforms
pros.example: a published mean traced to the filtered subset and the exclusion rule that produced it

pros.claim: Typed derivation separates legitimate transformation from undisclosed alteration
pros.example: relabeling a copy as a transformation reveals silent data edits

cons.claim: Column/row-level lineage is expensive and can explode in size
cons.example: tracking every cell derivation in a large matrix becomes unmanageable

cons.claim: Reconstructed lineage may be incomplete for legacy or manual steps
cons.example: a hand-edited spreadsheet step leaves a gap in the chain

failure_modes: lineage gaps treated as 'no transformation' rather than 'unknown'
intermediate artifacts discarded so derivation cannot be re-checked
acceptance_tests: lineage resolves from each published result to primary sources
every transformation has a typed derivation edge

nodes.definition: Make provenance FAIR: findable, accessible, interoperable, and reusable, with persistent identifiers, standard vocabularies, and machine-actionable provenance metadata.
contradictors: author who deposits data with no machine-readable provenance

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: FAIR maturity assessment or PID/vocabulary standards change

pros.claim: FAIR provenance lets machines resolve and reuse lineage without human mediation
pros.example: a crawler resolves a dataset PID and retrieves its PROV graph automatically

pros.claim: Persistent identifiers keep provenance links from rotting as systems change
pros.example: a derivation link survives a repository migration via stable PIDs

cons.claim: FAIR compliance is graded and partial; 'FAIR' is rarely binary
cons.example: a dataset is findable and accessible but not interoperable

cons.claim: PID and vocabulary choices can lock provenance into a fragile ecosystem
cons.example: reliance on a deprecated identifier scheme breaks resolution

failure_modes: assuming open-access equals FAIR
using non-resolvable local identifiers as PIDs
acceptance_tests: each entity/agent has a resolvable persistent identifier
provenance metadata validates against a standard vocabulary
revisit_triggers: FAIR principles or assessment rubric updated

nodes.definition: Maintain immutable, timestamped audit trails and content versioning for data, code, and decisions so any state and change is reconstructable and tamper-evident.

included: version control for data and code

contradictors: lab keeping a single overwritten master file with no history

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: an artifact is modified, a version scheme changes, or tamper-evidence is needed

pros.claim: Hash-based versioning makes silent post-hoc edits detectable
pros.example: a changed result hash no longer matches the registered version

pros.claim: Immutable logs let reviewers reconstruct exactly what was known and when
pros.example: an audit log shows a figure was altered after submission

cons.claim: Audit trails add overhead and can be circumvented if not enforced at source
cons.example: manual commit discipline lets edits bypass the log

cons.claim: Versioning data (vs code) is harder and tooling is immature
cons.example: large binary datasets are awkward to version meaningfully

failure_modes: audit log writable/editable by the audited party
versions without content hashes so tampering is invisible
acceptance_tests: every artifact version has an immutable timestamp and content hash
the audit log is append-only and independently verifiable
revisit_triggers: new artifact class brought under audit

nodes.definition: Assess and enable computational reproducibility: same data plus same code yields the same results, via environment capture, deterministic pipelines, and re-execution.
contradictors: author who shares results but not the executable environment

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: code, data, or computational environment changes

pros.claim: Captured environments make 'same data same code' re-runnable years later
pros.example: a container reproduces a 2019 analysis bit-for-bit in 2026

pros.claim: Reproducibility is a precondition for trusting any derived claim
pros.example: an irreproducible pipeline blocks downstream meta-analysis inclusion

cons.claim: Bitwise reproducibility is fragile under hardware, RNG, and float nondeterminism
cons.example: GPU nondeterminism breaks exact result equivalence

cons.claim: Reproducible does not mean correct or valid
cons.example: a reproducible but methodologically flawed result is still wrong

failure_modes: equating reproducibility with scientific validity
missing seeds/lockfiles so re-execution diverges
acceptance_tests: the pipeline re-executes from captured environment without manual fixes
result equivalence is checked against a documented tolerance

nodes.definition: Plan and appraise replication: re-collecting data or re-running studies to test whether findings hold, distinguishing direct, conceptual, and reproduction studies.
contradictors: researcher who treats a single failed replication as definitive refutation

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: replication typology, success criteria, or evidential weight rules change

pros.claim: Typed replication separates 'same finding' from 'same method', avoiding false equivalence
pros.example: a conceptual replication failure does not prove a direct-replication failure

pros.claim: Pre-specified success criteria stop post-hoc reinterpretation of replication outcomes
pros.example: a prediction interval set in advance defines replication success

cons.claim: Replications are under-powered and rarely funded, biasing the evidence base
cons.example: an under-powered replication yields an uninformative null

cons.claim: 'Failed' replication conflates true null with low power or hidden moderators
cons.example: a null is mislabeled refutation despite a moderator difference

failure_modes: treating non-significant replication as proof of no effect
mixing conceptual and direct replications in success counts
acceptance_tests: replication type is declared before outcome interpretation
success criteria are pre-specified and applied as written

nodes.definition: Specify and timestamp hypotheses, design, and analysis plans before data collection or access to separate confirmatory from exploratory work.
contradictors: author who registers vaguely then claims any result as confirmatory

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the analysis plan, hypotheses, or registry record change

pros.claim: Timestamped preregistration makes p-hacking and HARKing detectable by comparison
pros.example: a result not in the plan is correctly flagged exploratory

pros.claim: Clear confirmatory/exploratory split protects inferential validity
pros.example: only pre-specified tests carry confirmatory error control

cons.claim: Vague or gameable preregistrations provide false assurance
cons.example: an under-specified plan permits many 'confirmatory' analyses

cons.claim: Rigid plans can deter legitimate, well-flagged exploration
cons.example: a defensible deviation is penalized as a violation

failure_modes: registering after seeing data (preregistration theater)
unlogged deviations presented as planned
acceptance_tests: preregistration timestamp precedes data access
every deviation from the plan is logged with rationale

nodes.definition: Use registered-report review where the plan is peer-reviewed and accepted in principle before results, reducing publication bias and outcome-dependent acceptance.
contradictors: editor who accepts only positive-result manuscripts

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: stage-1 protocol or in-principle acceptance terms change

pros.claim: Outcome-independent acceptance removes the incentive to chase significant results
pros.example: a null result is published because the question and method were sound

pros.claim: Stage-1 review catches design flaws before resources are spent
pros.example: reviewers fix an underpowered design before data collection

cons.claim: Registered reports are slow and not offered by most venues
cons.example: a time-sensitive study cannot wait for stage-1 review

cons.claim: In-principle acceptance can be undermined by undisclosed deviations
cons.example: authors quietly change analyses after acceptance

failure_modes: treating in-principle acceptance as final without stage-2 checks
allowing outcome-dependent edits post-acceptance
acceptance_tests: in-principle acceptance is recorded before results exist
stage-2 review verifies adherence to the accepted protocol

nodes.definition: Detect questionable research practices such as p-hacking, HARKing, selective reporting, and optional stopping that fall short of misconduct but distort the record.
contradictors: author who frames exploratory mining as confirmatory testing

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: reporting standards, QRP definitions, or comparison baselines change

pros.claim: Comparing protocol to report exposes selective reporting and HARKing
pros.example: an outcome in the paper but absent from the registry is flagged

pros.claim: QRP signals catch distortion that misconduct definitions miss
pros.example: a p just below 0.05 cluster signals likely p-hacking

cons.claim: QRP signals are probabilistic, not proof; benign explanations exist
cons.example: a forking path can reflect legitimate robustness checks

cons.claim: Without a preregistration, QRP detection is weak and contestable
cons.example: no baseline plan means HARKing cannot be demonstrated

failure_modes: labeling a QRP signal as proven misconduct
ignoring legitimate exploratory framing
acceptance_tests: each QRP flag cites a concrete protocol-to-report discrepancy or statistical signal
flags are severity-graded and not asserted as misconduct

nodes.definition: Assess the three core misconduct categories (fabrication, falsification, plagiarism) using definitional criteria, image/data forensics signals, and similarity evidence.
contradictors: reviewer who declares misconduct from a single anomaly without corroboration

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: definitional standard, forensic method, or corroborating evidence changes

pros.claim: Definition-anchored assessment separates FFP from honest error and QRPs
pros.example: an inadvertent duplication is not classed as falsification

pros.claim: Corroborated forensic and similarity signals build a defensible finding
pros.example: duplicated bands plus inconsistent raw files jointly indicate falsification

cons.claim: Misconduct findings are high-stakes and error-prone; false positives harm careers
cons.example: an artifact compression artifact is mistaken for image splicing

cons.claim: Intent is hard to establish and often outside the analyst's remit
cons.example: manipulation is evident but intent cannot be proven

failure_modes: inferring intent from a single statistical anomaly
conflating plagiarism similarity with paraphrase
acceptance_tests: each FFP claim maps to a definitional criterion and corroborating evidence
honest-error and QRP alternatives are explicitly excluded
human review sign-off is recorded

nodes.definition: Decide and execute corrections, expressions of concern, or retractions using COPE/journal flowcharts, proportionate to error type, severity, and integrity of the record.

included: correction vs expression-of-concern vs retraction selection

contradictors: editor who silently removes a paper instead of issuing a notice

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: COPE/journal policy, severity assessment, or new evidence changes

pros.claim: Proportionate action keeps the literature trustworthy without over-retracting honest error
pros.example: an honest-error correction preserves a sound paper while fixing a figure

pros.claim: Transparent retraction notices let downstream users reassess citing work
pros.example: a notice stating the reason lets a meta-analysis exclude the study

cons.claim: Retraction is largely irreversible and reputationally severe
cons.example: a wrongful retraction is hard to undo and damages authors

cons.claim: Opaque or blame-free notices leave the record ambiguous
cons.example: 'the authors wish to retract' hides whether misconduct occurred

failure_modes: retracting without a transparent reason
correcting an article that warrants retraction
acceptance_tests: corrective action follows the applicable COPE/ICMJE flowchart
the notice states the reason and is linked to the original
irreversible retraction has human sign-off

nodes.definition: Continuously surveil the literature for retractions, corrections, and concerns (e.g., Retraction Watch, Crossref, PubPeer) and propagate status to citing and reusing work.
contradictors: analyst who cites papers without checking current retraction status

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: retraction feeds, citation graph, or propagation rules change

pros.claim: Continuous surveillance prevents citing or reusing already-retracted work
pros.example: an alert removes a retracted study from a draft review before submission

pros.claim: Status propagation flags downstream work resting on a retracted result
pros.example: a meta-analysis is re-run after an included trial is retracted

cons.claim: Retraction feeds are incomplete and lag the actual decision
cons.example: a retracted paper still appears valid for months in some indexes

cons.claim: PubPeer concerns are unverified and can include unfounded allegations
cons.example: an unsubstantiated comment triggers a false re-screen

failure_modes: treating absence from a feed as proof of integrity
propagating unverified allegations as retractions
acceptance_tests: each citing/reusing artifact carries current retraction status
new retractions trigger a re-screening worklist entry

nodes.definition: Establish first-class citation of datasets and software with persistent identifiers and credit metadata so provenance includes proper attribution and reuse tracking.
contradictors: author who reuses a dataset without citing it

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: data-citation standards or PID/credit metadata change

pros.claim: First-class data citation makes reuse and provenance attributable and countable
pros.example: a dataset DOI lets reuse be tracked across many citing papers

pros.claim: Contributor-role metadata clarifies who is accountable for which artifact
pros.example: CRediT roles distinguish the data curator from the analyst

cons.claim: Data citation is inconsistently practiced and indexed
cons.example: a reused dataset is acknowledged in text but not formally cited

cons.claim: PID granularity mismatches can misattribute versions
cons.example: citing a dataset without a version pins the wrong snapshot

failure_modes: citing data informally so reuse is uncountable
omitting dataset version in the citation
acceptance_tests: each reused dataset/software has a resolvable citation with version
contributor roles are recorded for cited artifacts

nodes.definition: Query the provenance graph and audit trails to answer integrity questions: what produced this result, who is accountable, and where the chain is broken or altered.
contradictors: auditor who trusts a result without querying its lineage

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: provenance graph, audit trail, or integrity question set changes

pros.claim: Querying lineage answers 'what produced this' deterministically
pros.example: a SPARQL query returns the exact source and activity for a figure

pros.claim: Gap detection surfaces unprovenanced or altered steps for review
pros.example: a missing wasGeneratedBy edge marks an unaccountable result

cons.claim: Query answers are only as complete as the captured provenance
cons.example: a gap in lineage yields an inconclusive accountability answer

cons.claim: Complex queries can mislead if PROV semantics are misread
cons.example: confusing used with wasDerivedFrom returns wrong sources

failure_modes: trusting query results over an incomplete provenance graph
misreading PROV relations in queries
acceptance_tests: each integrity question maps to a reproducible provenance query
provenance gaps are enumerated rather than silently ignored

nodes.definition: Triage and prioritize provenance/integrity concerns by severity, irreversibility, and downstream impact to route effort to the highest-risk artifacts first.

included: routing to appraisal vs corrective action

contradictors: officer who processes concerns first-in-first-out regardless of severity

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: concern inventory, severity weights, or downstream impact changes

pros.claim: Severity-weighted triage focuses scarce review effort on the riskiest artifacts
pros.example: a critical-result concern is appraised before a cosmetic typo

pros.claim: Impact-aware routing prevents a high-reuse dataset error from lingering
pros.example: a widely reused dataset concern jumps the queue

cons.claim: Triage scores are heuristic and can mis-rank novel concern types
cons.example: a subtle systemic issue is under-scored as low severity

cons.claim: Over-triage can defer legitimate but low-severity corrections indefinitely
cons.example: minor corrections never reach the top of the queue

failure_modes: first-in-first-out processing ignoring severity
under-weighting downstream reuse impact
acceptance_tests: each concern has a documented severity, irreversibility, and impact score
queue order follows the triage score

nodes.definition: Govern the evidence behind every provenance and integrity claim: label provenance assertions, separate captured fact from inferred reconstruction, and bound certainty.

included: provenance-claim labeling (captured vs reconstructed vs inferred)

contradictors: analyst who states reconstructed lineage as captured fact

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: evidence labeling policy or claim-certainty thresholds change

pros.claim: Labeling captured vs reconstructed provenance prevents overclaiming integrity
pros.example: a reconstructed chain is marked low-certainty, not asserted as fact

pros.claim: Claim-to-evidence traceability makes every integrity assertion auditable
pros.example: each finding links to the forensic or lineage evidence behind it

cons.claim: Conservative labeling can understate strong but informal evidence
cons.example: robust circumstantial provenance is downgraded to 'inferred'

cons.claim: Labeling discipline adds process overhead reviewers may skip
cons.example: time pressure leads to unlabeled assertions

failure_modes: stating inferred lineage as captured fact
unlabeled or unsourced integrity claims
acceptance_tests: every provenance/integrity claim carries an evidence label and source
reconstructed claims are bounded and never stated as captured fact

nodes.definition: Distinguish honest error and good-faith disagreement from QRPs and misconduct, calibrating response to avoid both under- and over-reaction.
contradictors: reviewer who treats every error as presumptive misconduct

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: error/intent evidence, integrity standard, or author response changes

pros.claim: Separating honest error preserves trust and encourages self-correction
pros.example: an author-initiated correction is rewarded, not penalized

pros.claim: Proportionate response prevents chilling effects on legitimate research
pros.example: a minor good-faith error draws a correction, not a retraction

cons.claim: Intent is rarely observable and easily misjudged
cons.example: a careless but honest mistake is read as deliberate

cons.claim: Over-leniency can let patterned misconduct pass as 'error'
cons.example: repeated 'errors' all favoring the hypothesis are excused

failure_modes: assuming intent from outcome severity alone
excusing a pattern of one-directional 'errors'
acceptance_tests: classification cites criteria distinguishing error, QRP, and misconduct
response proportionality is justified and human-reviewed

nodes.definition: Validate the provenance/integrity assessment itself: completeness of lineage, reference integrity, label legality, and reproducibility of every integrity verdict.
contradictors: reviewer who accepts integrity verdicts without re-checking the chain

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a finding is repaired, evidence relabeled, or the lineage graph changes

pros.claim: Validating the audit itself catches dangling references and overclaims before action
pros.example: a verdict resting on a broken chain is blocked from issuing a retraction

pros.claim: Verdict reproducibility lets a second reviewer reach the same conclusion
pros.example: an independent reviewer reproduces the FFP finding from the same evidence

cons.claim: Validation cannot certify substantive correctness, only consistency
cons.example: a self-consistent dossier can still rest on a flawed forensic read

cons.claim: Heavy validation can delay urgent corrective action
cons.example: a slow re-check delays a needed expression of concern

failure_modes: validating structure while ignoring substantive overclaim
skipping verdict reproduction for urgent cases
acceptance_tests: all references and labels pass an automated integrity check
each high-stakes verdict is independently reproducible from the dossier

edges.why_related: Modeling lineage needs the scoped object and standard.
edges.example: Adding an artifact re-anchors the graph.
edges.resolution_rule: scope dominates; rebuild graph on scope change

edges.why_related: Lineage tracking populates the PROV-O entity-activity graph.
edges.example: New relation type reshapes lineage.
edges.resolution_rule: model dominates; re-type lineage on model change

edges.why_related: FAIR packaging consumes the typed lineage trace.
edges.example: A new source needs a new PID.
edges.resolution_rule: lineage dominates; re-package on lineage change

edges.why_related: FAIR metadata reuses PROV-O entities and agents.
edges.example: Vocabulary migration re-maps entities.
edges.resolution_rule: model dominates; re-map vocabulary on change

edges.why_related: Versioning anchors each lineage step to an immutable version.
edges.example: A new transform needs a new version.
edges.resolution_rule: lineage dominates; version each step

edges.why_related: Reproduction needs versioned code, data, and environment.
edges.example: A dependency bump breaks re-run.
edges.resolution_rule: versioning dominates; re-pin on change

edges.why_related: Computational reproduction precedes empirical replication planning.
edges.example: An irreproducible pipeline taints replication.
edges.resolution_rule: reproduce first; replicate after equivalence

edges.why_related: Preregistration plan is scoped to the framed question.
edges.example: Scope change rewrites hypotheses.
edges.resolution_rule: scope dominates; re-register on scope change

edges.why_related: Registered reports build on a timestamped preregistration.
edges.example: A plan edit reopens stage-1.
edges.resolution_rule: preregistration dominates; re-review on edit

edges.why_related: QRP detection compares reports against the registered plan.
edges.benefit_of_coupling: A baseline plan makes HARKing detectable.
edges.example: Plan absence removes the comparison baseline.
edges.resolution_rule: preregistration dominates as baseline; flag exploratory absent plan

edges.why_related: FFP forensics needs immutable raw versions to compare.
edges.example: Overwritten raw files prevent falsification check.
edges.resolution_rule: versioning dominates; require raw versions before FFP finding

edges.why_related: QRP screening precedes and informs FFP assessment.
edges.benefit_of_coupling: QRP context separates distortion from fabrication.
edges.risk_of_conflict: Skipping QRP risks over-classing as misconduct.
edges.example: A p-hacking pattern is escalated as fabrication.
edges.resolution_rule: screen QRP first; escalate to FFP only with corroboration

edges.why_related: Corrective-action choice depends on FFP findings.
edges.risk_of_conflict: Acting before findings risks wrongful retraction.
edges.example: Premature retraction precedes the dossier.
edges.resolution_rule: findings dominate; no retraction before corroborated finding

edges.why_related: Action proportionality depends on the error-vs-misconduct call.
edges.example: Honest error wrongly retracted.
edges.resolution_rule: classification dominates; proportionate action follows

edges.why_related: Issued corrections feed the surveillance and propagation index.
edges.example: A retraction not propagated is re-cited.
edges.resolution_rule: decision dominates; propagate status after issuance

edges.why_related: Data citation reuses FAIR PIDs and credit metadata.
edges.benefit_of_coupling: PIDs make citations resolvable and countable.
edges.example: A local id cannot be cited persistently.
edges.resolution_rule: FAIR dominates; require resolvable PID for citation

edges.why_related: Querying audits the modeled provenance graph.
edges.benefit_of_coupling: A typed graph is queryable for accountability.
edges.example: A modeling error yields wrong query results.
edges.resolution_rule: model dominates; fix model before trusting queries

edges.why_related: Audit queries draw on the immutable trail.
edges.example: An edited log hides tampering from queries.
edges.resolution_rule: versioning dominates; require immutable trail for audit

edges.why_related: Governance labels the claims produced by audit queries.
edges.benefit_of_coupling: Labels bound certainty of audit results.
edges.example: A gap-laden query result asserted as fact.
edges.resolution_rule: query dominates; label every audit claim

edges.why_related: Validation checks the governed claims and labels.
edges.example: An unlabeled claim reaches a verdict.
edges.resolution_rule: governance dominates; validate before verdict issuance

edges.why_related: Triage prioritizes concerns within the framed scope and standard.
edges.example: An out-of-scope concern jumps the queue.
edges.resolution_rule: scope dominates; re-triage on scope change

edges.why_related: Triage routes high-severity concerns into FFP assessment first.
edges.example: A critical concern queued behind a typo.
edges.resolution_rule: triage order dominates; high severity first

edges.why_related: Triage routes lower-severity concerns into QRP screening.
edges.example: A minor concern over-escalated to FFP.
edges.resolution_rule: triage order dominates; route by severity

edges.why_related: Validation gates irreversible corrective action.
edges.benefit_of_coupling: No retraction issues on an unvalidated dossier.
edges.example: An urgent concern waits on full validation.
edges.resolution_rule: validation gates retraction; expedited path needs human sign-off

edges.why_related: Governance bounds how strongly FFP claims may be stated.
edges.risk_of_conflict: Strict bounds can understate strong evidence.
edges.example: A corroborated finding softened to 'concern'.
edges.resolution_rule: governance bounds claim strength; escalate via human review

edges.why_related: Versioned originals bound what counts as a faithful replication target.
edges.benefit_of_coupling: Pinned originals define the replication baseline.
edges.example: Replicating an unspecified version.
edges.resolution_rule: versioning bounds the target; pin the original

edges.why_related: Full reproducibility capture pressures the scoped effort budget.
edges.example: Bitwise capture demanded for every artifact in scope.
edges.resolution_rule: scope dominates; capture proportional to artifact risk

edges.why_related: Open FAIR reuse can tension with immutable, access-controlled audit.
edges.benefit_of_coupling: Both serve trust from different angles.
edges.example: FAIR openness exposes audit internals.
edges.resolution_rule: audit integrity dominates for sensitive trails; FAIR for public entities

edges.why_related: Rigid preregistration can tension with adaptive replication design.
edges.example: A justified replication deviation flagged as a QRP.
edges.resolution_rule: preregistration dominates; pre-specify allowed adaptivity

edges.why_related: Pressure to retract can override the honest-error distinction.
edges.example: An honest error retracted to look decisive.
edges.resolution_rule: honest-error distinction dominates; retract only on misconduct or fatal error

edges.why_related: Fast surveillance alerts can tension with governed, labeled claims.
edges.benefit_of_coupling: Both keep the record current and honest.
edges.example: An unverified PubPeer comment propagated as fact.
edges.resolution_rule: governance dominates; label surveillance items by verification status

edges.why_related: QRP flags can be misread as intent, tensioning the error distinction.
edges.example: A forking-path flag treated as deliberate manipulation.
edges.resolution_rule: honest-error distinction dominates; QRP flag is signal not verdict

edges.why_related: Validation defects trigger revisiting the provenance model.
edges.benefit_of_coupling: Closes the loop on modeling errors.
edges.example: A dangling entity sends the model back for repair.
edges.resolution_rule: revisit model on validation fail; stop after defects clear or 5 iterations

edges.why_related: A new retraction can trigger re-replication or re-synthesis.
edges.example: A retracted trial triggers re-running a synthesis.
edges.resolution_rule: revisit on new retraction; stop when status stabilizes or 3 iterations

edges.why_related: QRP findings trigger stricter future preregistration.
edges.example: HARKing detection prompts tighter pre-specification.
edges.resolution_rule: revisit preregistration practice on systemic QRP; stop after policy update

edges.why_related: Query-detected gaps trigger lineage re-capture.
edges.example: A missing derivation edge sends lineage back for repair.
edges.resolution_rule: revisit lineage on detected gap; stop when gaps resolved or 3 iterations

edges.why_related: Both probe whether findings hold under re-execution or re-collection.
edges.example: Computational reproduction confused with empirical replication.
edges.resolution_rule: keep distinct; reproduction=same data/code, replication=new data

edges.why_related: Both rely on persistent identifiers for attribution and reuse.
edges.risk_of_conflict: Treating citation as full FAIR is wrong.
edges.example: Data citation assumed to satisfy all FAIR facets.
edges.resolution_rule: keep distinct; citation is one FAIR-enabled practice

conflict_axes.trigger: full bitwise capture demanded for every artifact regardless of risk
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: capture depth is proportional to artifact risk and reuse, bounded by declared scope
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: capture cost threatens completing any high-risk artifact
conflict_axes.example: a low-reuse intermediate gets lightweight capture while a key result is fully containerized

conflict_axes.trigger: open reuse exposes sensitive audit internals
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: audit integrity dominates for sensitive trails; FAIR openness governs public entities and metadata
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: openness would expose information enabling tampering
conflict_axes.example: public PROV metadata is open while raw audit logs stay access-controlled

conflict_axes.trigger: a justified design adaptation conflicts with the registered plan
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: preregistration dominates inference, but allowed adaptivity must be pre-specified and deviations logged
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: an unplanned but defensible deviation affects a confirmatory test
conflict_axes.example: a sequential-analysis stopping rule is pre-registered to permit adaptive stopping

conflict_axes.trigger: pressure to retract before the error-vs-misconduct call is settled
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: retract only for misconduct or a fatal, uncorrectable error; honest error gets a correction
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: a retraction is proposed for an output classed as honest error
conflict_axes.example: an author-disclosed coding error yields a correction, not a retraction

conflict_axes.trigger: unverified post-publication critique is propagated quickly
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: surveillance items are labeled by verification status; only verified retractions propagate as fact
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: an unverified allegation would alter a downstream citation's status
conflict_axes.example: a PubPeer comment is logged as 'unverified concern' rather than a retraction

conflict_axes.trigger: a QRP statistical signal is read as deliberate manipulation
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: QRP signals are evidence, not verdicts; intent requires corroboration and human review
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: a single signal is used to assert intent or misconduct
conflict_axes.example: a cluster of p-values near 0.05 is flagged but not declared fabrication

conflict_axes.trigger: cell-level lineage demanded across a large dataset
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: granularity follows artifact risk; high-risk results get finer lineage, low-risk get coarse
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: capture cost blocks finishing a high-risk lineage
conflict_axes.example: a key effect gets row-level lineage while a sanity-check table gets dataset-level

conflict_axes.trigger: reconstructed lineage is asserted as captured fact
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: reconstructed provenance is labeled and certainty-bounded; never stated as captured
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: a reconstructed chain would support an irreversible action
conflict_axes.example: a retroactively inferred derivation is marked 'reconstructed, low certainty'

conflict_axes.trigger: an urgent concern pressures issuing action before full validation
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: validation gates irreversible action; an expedited path requires explicit human sign-off and a decision record
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: a retraction would issue on an unvalidated dossier
conflict_axes.example: an expression of concern is issued first while validation completes

edge_cases.trigger: an edge or dependency references a node ID that does not exist
edge_cases.failure_mode: dangling reference breaks the provenance graph
edge_cases.example: validator reports an unresolved edge endpoint
edge_cases.detection_method: reference validator over edges, dependencies, and refs
resolution: repair the reference to a valid node id

edge_cases.trigger: PROV-O typing diverges from the agreed model across artifacts
edge_cases.example: one artifact uses wasDerivedFrom where another uses used for the same step
edge_cases.detection_method: schema-conformance check against the PROV-O profile

edge_cases.trigger: a reconstructed or heuristic provenance claim is stated as captured fact
edge_cases.failure_mode: overclaimed certainty drives a wrongful integrity verdict
edge_cases.example: an inferred derivation chain is asserted as logged provenance
edge_cases.detection_method: label audit comparing claim labels to evidence type

edge_cases.trigger: a single node bundles fabrication, falsification, and plagiarism plus adjudication
edge_cases.failure_mode: node too large for one bounded reasoning session
edge_cases.example: FFP assessment also tries to decide sanctions

edge_cases.trigger: a high-risk node lacks acceptance tests or human review
edge_cases.failure_mode: irreversible action without a verification gate
edge_cases.example: a retraction node with no acceptance tests
edge_cases.detection_method: high-risk obligation check (risk>=0.80 needs tests + human_review)

edge_cases.trigger: a corrective decision is hard-locked before validation and review pass
edge_cases.example: a retraction notice locked before the dossier is validated
edge_cases.detection_method: lock-state gate check against validation and review status

edge_cases.trigger: validation-model feedback loops without a stop condition
edge_cases.example: each re-model introduces a new minor defect

edge_cases.trigger: a tradeoff is encoded as a dependency instead of a conflict
edge_cases.failure_mode: priority and gating logic become wrong
edge_cases.example: retraction-vs-error tension modeled as a prerequisite
resolution: convert to conflict edge with resolution_rule

edge_cases.trigger: a dependent node is ordered before its prerequisite
edge_cases.example: FFP assessment ranked before scope framing
edge_cases.detection_method: topological check of priority_order against dependencies

edge_cases.trigger: retraction status is stale or a feed lags the actual decision
edge_cases.failure_mode: a retracted artifact is cited or reused as valid
edge_cases.example: a retracted dataset still shows active status in an index
edge_cases.detection_method: feed freshness check and cross-source reconciliation
resolution: flag status as uncertain pending verification

edge_cases.trigger: a handoff artifact omits environment or lineage needed downstream
edge_cases.failure_mode: the next session cannot reproduce or audit
edge_cases.example: a reproduction package ships without the lockfile

edge_cases.trigger: an observed/experimentally_validated label is used without data
edge_cases.failure_mode: illegal evidence label inflates apparent certainty
edge_cases.detection_method: evidence-label legality audit (no observed without data)

workflow.objective: fix object-of-study, integrity standard, decision context, and triage priority
entry_criteria: integrity concern or provenance question received
acceptance_tests: object, unit, standard, and decision context documented
queue ordered by severity
workflow.do_first_because: scope, standard, and triage must precede all capture and appraisal to prevent rework

workflow.objective: build the PROV-O graph and typed end-to-end lineage
acceptance_tests: every output has wasGeneratedBy and wasAttributedTo
lineage resolves to primary sources
exit_criteria: graph and lineage complete or gaps enumerated
workflow.do_first_because: a typed provenance graph underpins all querying, FAIR packaging, and audit

workflow.objective: version artifacts immutably and make provenance FAIR and citable
acceptance_tests: each version has timestamp and content hash
each entity has a resolvable PID
reused data is cited with version
workflow.do_first_because: immutable versions and PIDs must exist before reproducibility and audit queries

workflow.objective: re-execute analyses from captured environments and verify result equivalence
acceptance_tests: pipeline re-executes without manual fixes
equivalence checked against documented tolerance
workflow.do_first_because: reproducibility is a precondition for trusting derived claims and planning replication

workflow.objective: establish confirmatory/exploratory demarcation and replication plan
acceptance_tests: preregistration timestamp precedes data access
replication success criteria pre-specified
workflow.do_first_because: a timestamped plan is the baseline that makes QRP detection possible

workflow.objective: screen for p-hacking, HARKing, selective reporting, and optional stopping
entry_criteria: preregistration baseline available or absence noted
acceptance_tests: each flag cites a concrete discrepancy or signal
flags are severity-graded, not asserted as misconduct
workflow.do_first_because: QRP context must precede misconduct assessment to avoid over-classification

workflow.objective: assess FFP with corroboration and distinguish honest error from misconduct
acceptance_tests: each FFP claim maps to a definitional criterion and corroborating evidence
honest-error and QRP alternatives explicitly excluded
human review sign-off recorded
workflow.do_first_because: corroborated findings must precede any irreversible corrective action

workflow.objective: query lineage to answer integrity questions and label every claim
entry_criteria: PROV-O graph and audit trail available
acceptance_tests: each integrity question maps to a reproducible query
every claim carries an evidence label and source
workflow.do_first_because: governed, labeled claims must precede validation and corrective action

workflow.objective: validate completeness, references, labels, and verdict reproducibility
acceptance_tests: all references and labels pass automated checks
each high-stakes verdict is independently reproducible
workflow.do_first_because: validation must gate irreversible corrective action

workflow.objective: issue proportionate corrective action and propagate status downstream
acceptance_tests: corrective action follows the applicable flowchart
notice states the reason and links to the original
irreversible retraction has human sign-off
workflow.do_first_because: corrective action is last because it is irreversible and gated by all prior validation

priority_rationale.notes: frozen scope and standard gate all capture and appraisal
severity routing focuses effort on the riskiest artifacts
typed graph underpins lineage, FAIR, and audit
lineage feeds versioning and FAIR packaging
immutable versions are required for reproduction and forensics
FAIR PIDs enable citation and reuse
audit queries produce the claims to be governed
irreversible action issued only after all gates pass

dominance_rules.rule: risk over speed: never skip corroboration for a misconduct finding to save time
dominance_rules.required_action: retain corroboration and human review for FFP
dominance_rules.example: a rushed retraction is held until the dossier is corroborated

dominance_rules.trigger: value ordering conflicts with dependency precedence
dominance_rules.rule: dependency order over value order: do not appraise before scope and provenance exist
dominance_rules.required_action: sequence by dependency, not perceived value
dominance_rules.example: FFP assessment waits for the PROV graph and raw versions

dominance_rules.rule: evidence label over numeric precision: a precise score never upgrades a heuristic label
dominance_rules.required_action: keep labels tied to evidence type

dominance_rules.trigger: pressure to lock a verdict before QA
dominance_rules.rule: QA over lock: no hard lock before validation passes
dominance_rules.required_action: run validation before any hard lock
dominance_rules.example: a retraction notice is not locked before ART_VALID

dominance_rules.rule: human review over automation for retraction and misconduct findings
dominance_rules.required_action: route high-risk verdicts to human sign-off
dominance_rules.example: an automated retraction suggestion requires editor approval

dominance_rules.rule: schema stability over population volume: keep PROV-O typing consistent
dominance_rules.example: a new artifact conforms to the agreed PROV profile

dominance_rules.rule: JSON validity over prose quality: machine-parseable output dominates
dominance_rules.example: no markdown or commentary leaks into the KB

dominance_rules.trigger: an unsupported integrity claim is convenient
dominance_rules.rule: source grounding over unsupported claims: every claim cites evidence
dominance_rules.required_action: attach evidence_refs and labels to all claims
dominance_rules.example: a reconstructed chain is labeled and sourced, not asserted

dominance_rules.trigger: density tempts exceeding the working budget
dominance_rules.rule: context budget over excessive density: reduce weak edges first
dominance_rules.required_action: trim weak similarity edges before core content
dominance_rules.example: low-value similarity edges removed before nodes

dominance_rules.trigger: local optimization conflicts with anti-rework order
dominance_rules.rule: anti-rework sequencing over local optimization: stabilize foundations first
dominance_rules.example: versioning is finalized before reproduction is attempted

dominance_rules.trigger: intent is inferred to look decisive
dominance_rules.rule: honest-error distinction over intent inference: signals are evidence, not verdicts
dominance_rules.required_action: require corroboration and human review for intent
dominance_rules.example: a QRP flag is not stated as deliberate fabrication

anti_rework_rules.rule: resolve object-of-study and standard before scope lock
anti_rework_rules.rationale: re-scoping invalidates all downstream capture and appraisal
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: appraisal started without a fixed standard
anti_rework_rules.example: FFP work begun before the integrity standard was named

anti_rework_rules.rule: fix competency questions before populating the provenance model
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: graph built without target integrity questions
anti_rework_rules.example: modeling lineage no audit query needs

anti_rework_rules.rule: establish source registry and labels before any evidence claim
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: a claim lacks an evidence label
anti_rework_rules.example: an integrity assertion with no source ref

anti_rework_rules.rule: freeze scope before building the provenance schema
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: graph typing changed after artifacts added
anti_rework_rules.example: a new object expands the graph mid-build

anti_rework_rules.rule: agree the PROV-O model before populating lineage
establish the preregistration baseline before QRP detection
anti_rework_rules.rationale: no baseline means HARKing cannot be shown
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: QRP flags without a comparison plan
anti_rework_rules.example: selective-reporting claim with no registered plan

anti_rework_rules.rationale: skipping QRP risks over-classifying as misconduct
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: a QRP signal escalated directly to fabrication

anti_rework_rules.rule: corroborate findings before any corrective action
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: retraction proposed before the dossier is complete

anti_rework_rules.rule: validate the dossier before hard-locking a decision
anti_rework_rules.rationale: unvalidated verdicts are unsafe to finalize

anti_rework_rules.rule: produce a handoff artifact after every major step
anti_rework_rules.rationale: missing handoffs force the next session to redo work

anti_rework_rules.rule: complete the traceability matrix before hard lock
anti_rework_rules.rationale: untraced claims cannot be safely finalized
anti_rework_rules.example: a verdict with no evidence linkage
